# Michigan Law Review

> A peer-reviewed law journal publishing rigorous legal scholarship across constitutional, administrative, antitrust, and emerging technology law domains.

Michigan Law Review is a student-run academic journal affiliated with the University of Michigan Law School. It publishes original legal scholarship, maintains an extensive archive of law review articles, and operates MLR Online for contemporary legal commentary.

## Key Topics

- Constitutional Law
- Administrative Law
- Antitrust Law
- Defamation Law
- Indian Law
- Cryptocurrency Law
- Deepfakes
- Sherman Act
- Legal Scholarship
- Supreme Court
- Establishment Clause
- Tribal Sovereignty
- Regulatory Policy
- AI-Generated Content
- Religious Freedom

## About & Submissions

- [About Us](https://michiganlawreview.org/about-us): Mission and student-run editorial structure of Michigan Law Review
- [Submissions](https://michiganlawreview.org/submissions): Submission guidelines for articles using Scholastica portal and citation standards
- [Subscribe](https://michiganlawreview.org/subscribe): Subscription information and contact details for Michigan Law Review publications

## Featured Articles & Recent Publications

- [Crypto Kleptocracy](https://michiganlawreview.org/crypto-kleptocracy): Article examining cryptocurrency corruption and regulatory issues in Trump Administration
- [Religious Riders and the Sherman Act](https://michiganlawreview.org/journal/religious-riders-and-the-sherman-act): Legal analysis of religious exemptions and antitrust law regarding healthcare providers
- [Pornographic Deepfakes and Ugly Social Facts: The Costs of a Normative Approach to Defamation](https://michiganlawreview.org/journal/pornographic-deepfakes-and-ugly-social-facts-the-costs-of-a-normative-approach-to-defamation): Article analyzing defamation law implications of AI-generated deepfakes and reputational harm
- [Courts of Indian Offenses, Courts of Indian Resistance](https://michiganlawreview.org/journal/courts-of-indian-offenses-courts-of-indian-resistance): Historical analysis of tribal courts and Native American legal institutions and sovereignty
- [Ten Commandments Cases: Learning from Reformation Coercion](https://michiganlawreview.org/ten-commandments-cases-learning-from-reformation-coercion): Constitutional law article on Establishment Clause and religious freedom using historical analysis
- [The Federal General Counsel, Law, and Our Democracy at a Crossroads](https://michiganlawreview.org/the-federal-general-counsel-law-and-our-democracy-at-a-crossroads): Administrative law article on federal general counsel roles in regulatory policy and democracy

## MLR Online Blog

- [MLR Online](https://michiganlawreview.org/blog): Blog featuring legal scholarship articles on constitutional and administrative law

- [Homepage](https://michiganlawreview.org): Recent publications across multiple legal domains
